description: Ask whether an action is allowed WITHOUT choosing the law yourself (NOMOS-SPEC-014). Describe where the act happens and who it involves; NOMOS works out from its signed registrar log which laws govern it, asks every one, and combines strictly: any deny denies, a yes needs every law. Prefer this over ask_authority whenever you do not already know which law applies: naming one law leaves out the others. Each law's own answer is a permanent, signed transcript (members[].query_id). If a fact that decides which law applies is missing, the answer is INSUFFICIENT_DATA with open_facts naming it: ask the user, never guess. A place the registrar does not cover is answered INSUFFICIENT_DATA, never as permission; say so plainly. Relay `coverage`: the registrar lists only its own laws, so other law may also apply.

action.description: Optional label for what is being done (e.g. "share_customer_data_with_analytics_vendor"), recorded on each transcript.

acts_for.description: Optional organisation the agent acts for.

agent_id.description: Optional stable name for the agent asking, recorded on each transcript.

context.description: The facts that decide which law applies. Codes: EU (an EU member state), QA (Qatar), AE (the UAE outside free zones with their own data law), DIFC, ADGM, QFC, US, SA, and so on.

established_in.description: Where the acting organisation is incorporated or established

output_used_in.description: Where any AI system output is used (the same as jurisdiction if no AI is involved)

subjects_in.description: Where the people the act concerns are located or resident

exchange_api_key.description: Exchange API key (nxk_...). Optional; needed only for licensed (paid) authorities.

inputs.description: Facts about the action itself, evaluated by every law that applies (e.g. {"processing_fair_and_transparent": true}). A law that needs a fact you did not give holds the answer open and names it.

purpose.description: Set "test" for test or evaluation queries: answered and sealed, but kept out of public history and counts.

name: ask_by_context

answered_under.description: The laws the answer was computed under

authorized.description: True only when every applicable law authorizes; never true over an empty set of laws

coverage.description: What the answer covers; relay it to the user

deciding_authorities.description: The laws that decided the verdict

escalations.description: Each law that requires approval, with its escalation

members.description: Each law's own answer, with its permanent transcript (query_id)

mode.description: "resolution": the laws were worked out from the context, not chosen by the caller

open_facts.description: Facts to supply when the answer is held open

resolution.description: How the laws were resolved (status, applicable, missing, proof with the log head consulted)

verdict.description: The strict combination of every applicable law's verdict
